item.title: Liberia says it's taking in 1,200 third-country US deportees
item.description: The government in Monrovia says the first batch of 20 people should arrive in Liberia on Thursday. The Trump administration has been seeking countries to take people it cannot send back to their countries of origin.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: India 'Cockroach' movement takes aim at government schools
item.description: The student protest movement is turning its grassroots network into a nationwide campaign to audit neglected government schools and pressure authorities to act.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why the US is going after the International Criminal Court
item.description: Marco Rubio, Donald Trump's secretary of state, has announced sanctions against two members of the International Criminal Court, including its president. Rubio's pressure on the court has far-reaching consequences.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Could Pakistan's jailed ex-PM Imran Khan make a new deal?
item.description: The imprisoned former prime minister of Pakistan could be moved to a hospital for medical treatment, ushering speculation over the possibility of new political negotiations.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Fact check: How do I spot fake social media accounts, bots and trolls?
item.description: If you are unsure whether to trust a message on TikTok or X, study its source. The following indicators can help you determine if you are dealing with a fake account, bot or troll.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
item.description: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: US: Meta hooked children, prosecutors say, as trial over social media harm begins
item.description: Four US states have taken Meta to court, accusing the social media giant of deliberately making Facebook and Instagram addictive for children. Meta has denied the charges.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: German Africa Prize goes to Kenyan social entrepreneur
item.description: Wawira Njiru organizes meals for hundreds of thousands of schoolchildren in Kenya, while at the same time supporting local farmers. For this, she is being honored by the German Africa Foundation.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Minors living alone on Ceuta's streets at risk of abuse
item.description: Several thousand unaccompanied minors have gathered in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave on the northern coast of Africa. Illness and abuse are rife, and the authorities admit they are overwhelmed.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Afghanistan: Only 5% of labor market are women under Taliban
item.description: The International Labour Organization estimates that only 5.1% of workers in Afghanistan are women, five years after the Taliban's return to power. That's less than a third of the proportion in 2019 and 2020.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Should India worry about the Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey pact?
item.description: A defense agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey brings Islamabad deeper into the security architecture of the Middle East. How is India planning to respond?
